constitution: PR #1641 — Wheel of Football grading constitution
gradingSemantic: CURRENT NFL ABILITY AT TIGHT END RIGHT NOW; position-normalized; receiving ability, separation/route value, hands, YAC, blocking, inline usefulness, versatility and ability to stay on the field across personnel packages. Receiving is important but does not mechanically override complete tight-end play. Not career greatness, fantasy value, draft status, projection, or short-streak production.

evidenceSnapshot.note: Week 4 incomplete. 2025 full-season evidence is the stronger baseline unless 2026 evidence is sufficiently meaningful. Injury/availability is separate from underlying ability. External rankings/grades are evidence only.
primarySources: Pro-Football-Reference 2025 receiving table and current player pages
NFL.com individual tight-end career/stat pages through Week 3/4 of 2026
PFF 2026 preseason tight-end rankings and 2025 positional grading/context

resolvedPressurePoints: Juwan Johnson grades 86 because 889 yards in 2025 plus 173 yards and three touchdowns through three 2026 games establish real receiving ability; weaker inline/blocking value keeps him below Pitts and the star group.

AJ Barner and Brenton Strange both reach 85 because their receiving production is paired with unusually strong run-blocking evidence; this prevents the system from becoming a receiving-only TE ranking.
Mark Andrews is 84. His 2025 career-low season matters more than career reputation, while a competent 2026 opening keeps him above the 82-83 group.
David Njoku and T.J. Hockenson remain at 82 because prior name value does not erase meaningful 2025 decline. Current evidence has not yet justified a rebound into the 84-85 range.
Colby Parkinson is 84 on a strong 2025 receiving/blocking season, but quiet 2026 usage prevents promotion into the 85 cluster.
Mason Taylor and Gunnar Helm sit at 79 because each has real NFL starter snaps but limited explosiveness; draft pedigree and youth projection are excluded.
Charlie Kolar ties Tommy Tremble at 78 because blocking value legitimately counts at tight end even without large receiving volume.

postGradeDistribution.note: Inspected only after grading; no grades were moved to shape the distribution.

runtimeBoundary: No production/runtime behavior changes. Runtime wiring, historical freezing and hidden reveal remain a later phase.
futureVersioning: Any future TE grade change must record previous grade, new grade, effective date, reason, and nearby anchor/peer comparison.
